name: FORTE neutrino search
full_name: Fast On-orbit Recording of Transient Events: neutrino analysis
summary: Data from the multipurpose FORTE radio satellite were searched for ultra-high-energy neutrino interactions in the Greenland ice sheet, providing early space-based limits on extreme-energy cosmic particle fluxes.
detection_principle: Coherent Cherenkov radio emission from a neutrino-induced shower in ice could be detected from orbit. Polarisation, ionospheric dispersion and geographical reconstruction help reject lightning and anthropogenic radio backgrounds.

sites.name: Low Earth orbit; Greenland ice target
sites.location: Satellite observations of the Greenland ice sheet; not a detector sited at LANL headquarters.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The neutrino search is a historical analysis of 1997–1999 satellite data; this status does not assert the spacecraft deorbit date.

timeline.event: Radio data used for the published neutrino search recorded.
Neutrino and model-dependent neutralino constraints published.

collaboration.name: FORTE neutrino search Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected participants named in the cited project publications.

results.summary: One event survived all selection cuts; the analysis treated it as background when setting flux limits. This was not claimed as a neutrino detection.

science_scope: Published limits are not neutrino detections. Instrument or exposure parameters refer to the explicitly named campaign; research prototypes and future designs are distinguished.
